- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast bias downward to avoid excessive sell-off.
- Model frequently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a small upward bias (e.g. +1–2%) to forecast peaks.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in early periods; delay mean-reversion correction until 15+ days into the forecast horizon.
- In 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period volatility; add a small volatility buffer (±1–3%) to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or trending.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-forecast, model often fails to adjust; trigger a “sentiment pivot” correction 3–5 days after sentiment change.
